headline: High: shared clipboard/files and MCP-enabled agent create prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict risks; ChatGPT Desktop’s default app/file access makes the pair unsafe without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while agent_b reads clipboard, uploaded files, and files from supported macOS apps. That creates a plausible content bridge where agent_a output can be pasted or surfaced into agent_b and treated as instructions. The interaction is documented only by profiles, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b clipboard or file inputs, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF agent_b is granted access to app-context or uploaded files from agent_a-generated content, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the agents.
Keep agent_a outputs in a plain-text quarantine file and review manually.
Turn off ChatGPT Desktop access to supported macOS apps for this workflow.
Use a separate workspace with no shared files.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging before any cross-agent transfer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures; agent_b reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and IDE code. Even without shared host write access, the pair can move sensitive material from agent_a into agent_b’s vendor-mediated backend through files or screenshots. The profiles support the pathway, but not a direct breach proof.
conditions: IF agent_a processes secrets or repository metadata and the result is pasted or uploaded into agent_b, leakage occurs.
IF agent_b is granted screen capture or file access to agent_a work products, sensitive content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not upload agent_a outputs containing secrets to agent_b.
Disable screen capture and app-context permissions in ChatGPT Desktop.
Use redacted copies of files before any transfer.
Store signatures and prompts in a separate vault.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before cross-agent sharing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b cannot write or modify git, so direct symmetric conflict is limited. However, both support multiple instances and can touch overlapping code/workspace artifacts through agent_b’s file and IDE access, creating contention and stale-state risk. This is more than low because the overlap is in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, git state races can occur.
IF agent_b reads files while agent_a rewrites them, stale or inconsistent artifacts can be produced.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other edits git state.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestrator-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate analysis, route/explain/build-agents outputs, and agent_b can consume files, screenshots, or IDE context. If agent_b treats agent_a’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream coding or documentation actions. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-produced text as source-of-truth without review, incorrect actions can propagate.
IF agent_a emits malformed or speculative outputs and agent_b forwards them into code or docs, the error cascades.
mitigations: Require human review before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Add a checklist to verify claims against source files.
Keep agent_a outputs labeled as untrusted drafts.
Use a second-pass validator for code or factual claims.
requires-engineering: implement structured provenance and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b is a closed-source desktop product with vendor-only egress and app/file/screen access, while agent_a is open-source and handles repository metadata and signatures. If regulated or residency-sensitive data from agent_a is transferred into agent_b, retention and jurisdiction controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or secrets from agent_a are sent into agent_b, compliance obligations may change.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to the shared data class, the vendor-only backend may conflict with local policy.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data from agent_a into agent_b.
Review ChatGPT Desktop retention settings before use.
Use synthetic or anonymized data for cross-agent tasks.
Keep residency-sensitive work in a separate environment.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and formal data-flow review.
